text:
alex: quick sync on allocation-lineage prototype. follow-up from last RFC, focusing on rollout/tradeoffs for compacting and offload affinity

morgan: missed the deep-dive. tl;dr?

alex: we attach a small origin token to allocations to capture "which logical pool" + intent. goal: use that to prefer co-locating lineage during compaction and to make evictor/admission affinity-informed

sasha: how small? adding metadata on the hot path worries me for tiny allocs

alex: design: 4 bytes token stored only for arenas that opt-in. default arenas remain zero-cost. for small arenas we have sampling mode instead of per-alloc writes

priya: sampling mode sounds safer. what's the sampler rate and lookup cost?

alex: prototype: sample 1/1024 allocations; we keep a sidecar map keyed by coarse buckets (64KB) -> token. on free, runtime checks sidecar to recover lineage for that region

morgan: sidecar lookup must be lock-light. coarse buckets mean fewer entries and fewer collisions. worst case: we miss lineage for tiny bins but that's acceptable

sasha: eviction/placement angle: if lineage suggests a preferred host pool, admission controller should prefer that pool. but avoid hard pinning or starvation

alex: yes. affinity is a soft score. we add weight to placement decisions, default weight 0.3. operator can tune per-tenant if they want stronger consolidation guarantees

priya: persistence question: sidecar must be checkpointed or reconstructible across restarts. enterprise customers will ask about consistency for Dedicated/Private deployments

morgan: plan: checkpoint hot buckets every Ns to compact snapshot with (bucket -> token). on restart, unlabeled buckets are treated as unknown and warmed lazily. we won't block startup on full rebuild

sasha: compaction planner: lineage helps by grouping blocks to move together, reducing scatter. but we need a grace window for rehoming so we don't thrash when affinity strengthens suddenly

alex: implement gradual rehomes: mark candidate lineage groups, schedule staged moves over control window (seconds). track moves and avoid triggering concurrent global compactions

infra-bot: ci: allocator/lineage branch perf: smoke tests pass (alloc-lin/ci#88)

alex: perf: sampling mode +0.4% median alloc latency, p99 +1.8%. memory overhead ~0.5% on mixed benchmarks. looks safe for opt-in rollout

morgan: suggest defaults: sample 1/2048 for small arenas, 64KB buckets, affinity weight 0.25. we should include a conservative default to minimize risk for self-serve users

priya: i'll own telemetry: add metrics sampled_allocs_total, sidecar_lookup_hits_total, lineage_compacted_bytes_total, affinity_move_ops_total. also trace compaction runs that used lineage as a primary heuristic

sasha: i'll run synthetic fragmentation sims to validate defaults and exercise worst-case patterns (high churn tiny allocs, long-lived fragments interleaved).

alex: roadmap items: 1) opt-in arena flag + sampling sidecar implementation; 2) admission controller affinity hook + weight config; 3) checkpoint format + lazy rebuild; 4) telemetry + sim results.

morgan: also add an operator knob for affinity aggressiveness per-tenant and per-node-liveness safety net (max concurrent lineage moves)

priya: noted. i'll sketch the checkpoint compact format: list of (bucket_start, token, last_seen_ts) compressed with simple delta encoding. we only persist buckets with recent activity to keep snapshots small

sasha: question for future RFC: can lineage tokens be extended to model-shard affinity (kv-caches + model shards)? seems promising but needs policy layer work

alex: added to follow-ups. ok to schedule a short tech-check next Wed to align on APIs? :thumbsup:

morgan: +1

priya: +1

sasha: +1

alex: filing notes -> https://go/internal/alloc-lineage/followup (TODO: finalize checkpoint proto)
